how_it_works.value: Five containerised services on Cloud Run behind one FastAPI gateway, declared in Terraform, running in a real GCP project with no emulators. Ingestion and compliance agents are Cloud Tasks workers (OIDC between them); state lives in Firestore, the audit trail in append-only BigQuery, documents and reports in Cloud Storage; a Cloud Scheduler job triggers Cloud Workflows for the weekly report. React dashboard with Firebase Auth on the front. Two decisions carry the design: tenant identity is taken only from verified JWT claims, never from a body or query parameter, so no code path can read across tenants; and rewriting an audit row needs both bigquery.tables.updateData and bigquery.jobs.create, so the writer identity holds the first and is denied the second - UPDATE and DELETE are unavailable to their own application rather than merely unused by it.

limits_they_disclosed.value: Prompting does not stop fabrication, so rules live in versioned YAML, a citation is mandatory in the output contract, prompt and model version are recorded against every check so a verdict can be reproduced, and when the model cannot ground a verdict it escalates instead of guessing. Their weekly report workflow existed, was scheduled and looked healthy in the console for three weeks without ever running: Cloud Scheduler was being refused with PERMISSION_DENIED into a log nobody read, and fixing it uncovered six defects behind each other (missing invoker role, doubled URL scheme, a request to a route the service does not serve, a hardcoded tenant list, a service account without Firestore access, a missing log-writer permission). They conclude the actual bug was that nothing was watching; there are now uptime checks and alerts on scheduler and workflow failures. Terraform silently dropped a hand-set environment variable because Cloud Run replaces its env list wholesale, which cost every platform admin console access at once; the same trap sat in payment flags where a default of false would have quietly removed PayPal credentials on a fresh checkout, so those variables are now required and a missing value stops the deploy. An unregistered domestic Razorpay account rejects international cards even in live mode, and Stripe's INR conversion fee turned a $50 audit into a much larger rupee figure at checkout, so they removed Stripe and use PayPal for international customers.

what_it_does.value: Upload a document (PDF, text, CSV or image). Routine documents auto-approve, edge cases escalate to a human reviewer with the reasoning attached, every decision is appended to an immutable audit trail, and a scheduled workflow produces weekly reports with a Gemini executive summary. Currently 16 rulesets, 88 rules, 12 jurisdiction profiles: NDIS and aged care in Australia, corporate compliance in India, and GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, LGPD, PDPA and POPIA.
